title: Cohomology properties of maps in (Cat) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of a section on the cohomology/homotopy of maps in (Cat), with Thomason/Quillen weak equivalences W. Grothendieck is assembling stability properties of the class W as a 'basic localizer'.

Theorem. Let I be a (filtered) ordered set. Let X, Y be small categories with increasing exhaustive filtrations (X_i)_{i in I} and (Y_i)_{i in I} by full subcategories that are all 'open' or all 'closed', with X = ∪X_i and Y = ∪Y_i. Let f: X → Y satisfy f(X_i) ⊂ Y_i, giving f_i: X_i → Y_i. If every f_i is a weak equivalence, then f is a weak equivalence.

Proof strategy (on this page):
1. Reduce to the case where I is an ordered set in which the relevant infima exist.
2. Encode the filtration as a functor φ: X → I, with φ(x) = Inf I(x), where I(x) = {i : x ∈ X_i}. The NB requires that φ(x) be the least element of I(x), so that I(x) = {j ≥ φ(x)}.
3. Functoriality: for α: x → y we have I(y) ⊂ I(x), since y ∈ X_i implies x ∈ X_i. So φ(x) ≤ φ(y), which defines φ(α). Here 'open' means each X_i is a sieve (crible), closed under sources of arrows.
4. Then X_i = φ^{-1}(I_{≤i}), i.e. x ∈ X_i iff φ(x) ≤ i iff i ∈ I(x).

The next page completes the argument. Since X_i = X_{/i} (comma over i) and f is a map over I, the f_i are the induced maps f_{/i}: X_{/i} → Y_{/i}. A Quillen Theorem A relative to a base ('L 3') then gives that f is a weak equivalence.

The rotated margin sketches the dual case of closed filtrations (cosieves). There one uses the reversed order and intersections, roughly 'Y_i = ∩_{j ≥ i} Y_j'.

The next page generalises the index from a poset to a category I. Filtrations become functors I → Ouv(X) commuting with the relevant colimits, with lim X_i ≅ X. It then derives corollaries:
- the analogue in presheaf categories A^,
- asphericity of a union of aspherical opens over a connected I,
- saturation of W.
errors: Defining φ(x) = Inf I(x) only gives a functor with X_i = φ^{-1}(I_{≤i}) if Inf I(x) actually belongs to I(x). This holds only when the filtration commutes with these infima, i.e. X_{inf} = ∩ X_i. Mere existence of infima in I is insufficient; the NB, and the next page's condition 'commutant aux dits lim', implicitly add this hypothesis.

The 'reduction to ordered sets with Inf' is only gestured at. For a general filtered I one must, for example, replace I by the lattice of sieves generated by the X_i, closed under intersections. This is not spelled out.

As written in the proof, filteredness is not used. The φ-argument plus Theorem A over I works for any such 'principal' filtration. Filteredness matters only if one wants to avoid the intersection-closure hypothesis.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard stability property of weak equivalences in Cat, proved by a neat but routine reduction to relative Theorem A. It belongs to Grothendieck's well-known development of localizers in Pursuing Stacks, later systematised by Cisinski and Maltsiniotis.

'On est ramené par [?]' likely reads 'par cofinalité' or 'par réduction'; uncertain.
